I spent most of last week in a meeting room that smelt of burnt coffee. Three days. We were trying to agree what "done" means for a policy nobody had read.

Here's the thing. Nobody disagreed with the policy. They just didn't know it existed, and when they found out, they asked who wrote it (me) and why it was eleven pages long (fair question).

So I cut it. Not to two pages; to one line on a sticky note: if you wouldn't email it to a stranger, don't paste it into a tool you don't control. You'd be amazed how far that gets you.

Is it perfect? No. Does it cover every edge case my legal team can dream up on a Friday afternoon? Also no. But people remember it, and they use it, and I've stopped getting the same three questions every Monday.

I think that's the bit we get wrong. We write rules for the auditor and then act surprised when the people doing the work ignore them. Write for the person at the desk. The auditor can have the appendix.
